subject: Decision criteria follow-up: latency / cost / deployment / procurement
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Liu <jason.liu@finova.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (decision criteria: latency / cost / deployment)

Hi Jason —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

Summary of Finova's decision criteria (as called out on the call):
- Latency: target 95th percentile end-to-end generation latency <= 200ms for short completions (<= 512 tokens).
- Cost: target per-token cost that keeps incremental infra cost < $0.002/token for cached/batched workloads (your words: "must be cost-competitive with current API spend").
- Deployment mode: preference for VPC/private control plane with customer-managed networking; open to starting on Dedicated reserved capacity if it speeds proof-of-concept and reduces procurement friction.
- SLA: commercial uptime SLO target 99.9% and a latency SLA for p50/p95; procurement will want clear rollback/fallback policies.

Procurement & stakeholder map we captured:
- Economic buyer: Priya Suresh (VP Product) — will own ROI/cost conversation.
- Security/legal: likely engaged for SOC2, data residency and KMS/HSM details. Rishi/Mike from your security team expected to review evidence.
- Procurement: Carlos Gomez — handles contracts/POs.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I will send a brief SOW + pricing options (Dedicated vs Private) and call out what meets your latency and cost targets.
2) Dev (cc'd) will share a short note on technical approach for hitting 200ms p95 (model variants, batching, and KV/prefix caching).
3) If procurement wants a kickoff, Carlos+Priya can propose times and we'll bring Legal/Security for a focused evidence session (SOC2 docs, network diagrams, data flow, KMS).

Attachments: discovery-notes.pdf (call notes + timestamps)

Would you add or correct anything above? If that looks right, I'll follow up with the SOW and pricing by Tuesday.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jason Liu <jason.liu@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@finova.com>, Carlos Gomez <carlos.gomez@finova.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (decision criteria: latency / cost / deployment)

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary, this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Economic buyer: yes, Priya will sign off on budget. She asked for a high-level ROI example (savings vs current vendor) in the SOW.
- Procurement: Carlos is the correct contact; typical PO timeline for us is ~4–6 weeks after SOW/contract if pricing and legal terms are standard.
- Security: our security lead (Rishi Malhotra, rishi.malhotra@finova.com) will need SOC2 Type II evidence and an architecture/data flow diagram; we prefer data residency in US regions for now.
- Deployment: Preference is VPC/private control plane, but Priya said they'd consider starting on Dedicated for speed if migration to Private is clearly defined and low-risk. Important: we need to understand what changes during migration (downtime, data movement, rekeying KMS).

Two quick asks:
1) Can you include a short section in the SOW that maps Dedicated -> Private migration steps and expected effort?
2) Can your engineering team confirm the 200ms p95 target on a 4k context with the models you recommend (or give realistic expectations if longer)?

I'll wait for the SOW and technical note. Proposed week-of-Aug 9 for procurement kickoff (Carlos will confirm).

Best,
Jason
Sr. Product Manager | Finova

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + next steps (decision criteria: latency / cost / deployment)

Marissa / Neha — quick technical write-up to include in the follow-up SOW / appendix: 

- Latency options: For p95 <= 200ms on short completions (<=512 tokens) we recommend a small ensemble: an optimized open decoder (quantized) hosted on Dedicated with continuous batching + prefix KV caching. On A100-equivalent hardware we've seen consistent p95s in the 120–180ms range for <512 token completions when using our runtime optimizations.
- 4k context note: p95 will increase with longer contexts due to KV cache growth; for 4k context we typically project p95 in 300–450ms range depending on model size; we can prune context and use streaming to mitigate.
- Migration path (Dedicated -> Private):
   * Data: customer data remains isolated; we support encrypted backups and controlled transfer.
   * KMS: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) on Private; Dedicated can be configured with separate keys per customer but migrating keys requires coordinated re-encryption steps (~1–2 business days of ops work).
   * Downtime: planned migration can be done with near-zero downtime using dual-write and traffic cutover; we will include runbook and backout steps.

Attaching redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx (pricing bands + estimated TCO for your expected throughput).

Happy to sync on a short tech call to walk through benchmarks.
—Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Liu <jason.liu@finova.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@finova.com>, Carlos Gomez <carlos.gomez@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: SOW + next steps (includes migration path + ROI example)

Hi Jason / Priya / Carlos —

Thanks for the clarifications. Attached is an initial SOW (SOW_v1.pdf) that includes:
- Two deployment options (Dedicated reserved capacity and Private VPC) with pricing bands and an ROI example comparing to an API-only vendor.
- A migration appendix that maps Dedicated -> Private steps, estimate of ops effort, key rotation notes, and expected downtime (near-zero planned, detailed runbook included).
- A tech appendix (excerpt from Dev) on latency expectations for <=512 token completions and 4k contexts.

We also created a HubSpot deal and included links for easy reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FIN-2026-0893

Next proposed actions:
1) Procurement kickoff: week of Aug 9 (Carlos to confirm availability).
2) Security evidence session: we can prepare SOC2 artifact pack and a network/dataflow diagram — propose Thu Aug 12 10:00 AM PT.
3) Technical benchmark call: optional, 30min with Dev and Neha to validate p95 numbers (we can run targeted tests against a sample payload).

If that looks good I'll send a DocuSign SOW after we confirm minor pricing items.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Jason Liu <jason.liu@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@finova.com>, Carlos Gomez <carlos.gomez@finova.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOW + next steps (includes migration path + ROI example)

Marissa — appreciate the fast turnaround and the level of detail. SOW looked good at a glance. A couple quick notes: 
- Priya appreciates the ROI example; she asked that you call out the expected payback period (we'll expect a 6–9 month payback target).
- Carlos: please confirm availability for procurement kickoff week of Aug 9 — Carlos, any day/time that week works for you?
- Rishi (cc'd) will review the SOC2/artifact pack and confirm whether a short recorded walkthrough is sufficient or if he needs a live evidence session.

Let's schedule the technical benchmark call for Aug 4 11:00 AM PT if that works for Dev/Neha — Jason (me) will have the short sample payload ready.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Jason
